productSettings.heading: Product settings
productSettings.safetyHelp: Extra days of stock kept in case sales jump or a delivery is late.
productSettings.minOrderHelp: The supplier's minimum order in units. Suggestions below it are raised to it.
productSettings.packSizeHelp: Units per case or pack. Suggestions are rounded up to whole packs.
productSettings.minStockHelp: Reorder when stock plus stock on the way falls to this. Leave empty to let the forecast decide.
productSettings.maxStockHelp: Orders fill stock up to this level. Leave empty to let the forecast decide.
productSettings.muteAlerts: Don't send alerts for this product
productSettings.muteAlertsHelp: Leaves it out of summary and real-time emails. Forecasts and the reorder list still include it.
productSettings.discontinuedHelp: Sell through what is left: no order suggestions, alerts, purchase plan or Flow triggers. It stays visible with its sell-out date, and it does not count toward the Free plan limit.
productSettings.referenceHelp: Until this product has {{count}} days of its own sales, its forecast borrows this product's sales rate, less and less as its own history grows.

settings.defaultsIntro: Used for products without their own lead time or supplier.

settings.leadTimeHelp: How long a reorder usually takes to arrive.
settings.alertsLocked: Get one summary email when products need reordering. Never more than one a day.

settings.frequencyHelp: One summary email, only when something needs attention.
settings.realtimeHelp: An email as soon as stock crosses a threshold. Changes are grouped into one email every 15 minutes, a product is mentioned at most once a week, at most 3 emails a day and never at night.
settings.realtimeOutOfStock: Only when a product sells out
settings.realtimeAll: When a product needs reordering or sells out

import.heading: Import suppliers from purchase orders
import.intro: Coming from Stocky? Stocky can't export suppliers, but its purchase orders show who supplies what. Upload them and we'll create your suppliers, link each product to the supplier you last ordered it from, and measure lead times from past deliveries.
import.stepExport: In Stocky, open Purchase orders (or Reports) and export them as CSV. Several files are fine.
import.stepUpload: Drop the files below. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
import.stepCheck: Check the suppliers and lead times we found, then import.
import.otherApps: Purchase order CSVs from other apps or spreadsheets work too, as long as they have a supplier column and a SKU, variant ID or product name column.
import.columnsHelp: We matched these columns automatically. Change any that look wrong.
import.missing: We couldn't find: {{fields}}. Choose the right columns below.

import.unmatched_other: {{count}} rows didn't match a product in your store (for example {{samples}}). They are skipped.

flow.heading: Shopify Flow
flow.intro: Start your own workflows from the forecast: post to Slack, tag products, create a task, email your team. Build them in the Shopify Flow app with these triggers. Each one fires once per change, never every night.
flow.locked: Start Shopify Flow workflows when a product needs reordering, is about to run out, or a supplier order is due.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what {{app}} (the "app") reads from your Shopify store, what it keeps, and how to have it deleted. The app is used by Shopify merchants; it has no contact with your customers.

reads.heading: What the app reads from Shopify
reads.products: titles, SKU, barcode, vendor, product type, price, unit cost, status.
reads.inventory: available and incoming quantities per location, and your locations.
reads.orders: only the quantity sold and returned of each variant, the order date and, for stores with several locations, which location fulfilled it, to build daily sales totals. The app never requests customer names, emails, addresses, phone numbers or payment details.
reads.store: shop domain, name, currency, time zone and contact email (used to email you when no alert email is set).

stores.heading: What the app stores
stores.sales: Daily sales totals per variant (units sold, units returned, end-of-day stock) for up to 400 days. Raw orders are not stored.
stores.catalog: Your product catalog details listed above, current stock levels, and the forecasts computed from them.
stores.entered: What you enter in the app: suppliers (name, email, lead time), settings, bundles and forecast adjustments.
stores.shop: Your shop domain, an encrypted Shopify access token, your plan and the email address you choose for alerts.
stores.emails: A log of emails the app sent for you (recipient, subject, date, delivery status; not the message), kept 180 days, and for purchase orders you email to a supplier, the products and quantities ordered.
stores.noCustomers: The app stores no personal data of your customers.
stores.noCustomersBody: Requests Shopify forwards on behalf of your customers (data requests, erasure requests) therefore have nothing to return or delete.

use.heading: How it is used
use.body: Only to provide the app: forecasting, reorder suggestions, the emails you turn on, and support. The data is not sold, shared for advertising, or used to train AI models. No tracking or advertising cookies are used; the app runs inside the Shopify admin and signs requests with Shopify session tokens.

providers.heading: Service providers
providers.body: The app runs on a hosting provider (servers and database), sends email through an email delivery provider, and reports technical errors (without customer data; access tokens are masked) to an internal monitoring channel. They process data only on our behalf to run the app.

retention.heading: Retention and deletion
retention.uninstall: When you uninstall the app, its access token is removed immediately and billing stops.
retention.erase: 48 hours after uninstall, Shopify asks the app to erase your shop's data and everything is deleted (sales totals, catalog, forecasts, suppliers, settings, email log). Reinstalling within those 48 hours keeps your data.
retention.sooner: To have your data deleted sooner, or for a copy of it, email

security.heading: Security
security.body: Traffic is encrypted (HTTPS). Access tokens are encrypted at rest. Webhooks from Shopify are verified by signature.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Questions or requests about your data:

support.title: Support
support.contact: Need help with {{app}}? Email us at
support.reply: We reply within one business day.

forecast.a: Every product has a "Why this number?" explanation: the sales windows used (7, 30 and 90 days), the out-of-stock days left out, seasonality, bundles, lead time and safety stock. You can adjust the sales rate, lead time and safety stock yourself.

noForecast.q: Why don't I see forecasts yet?
noForecast.a: Right after install the app imports your orders and stock in the background (a progress bar shows it). A store without orders gets forecasts once it starts selling; products without sales show "no sales yet".

stocky.q: I'm moving from Stocky. Can I keep my suppliers?
stocky.a: Yes. Export your purchase orders from Stocky as CSV and import them in Suppliers → Import from Stocky. The app creates your suppliers, links products and works out each supplier's lead time.

billing.q: How does billing work? Can I cancel anytime?
billing.a: Plans are a flat monthly or yearly price billed on your Shopify invoice: no share of your sales, no contract. Your price never goes up while you stay on your plan. Uninstalling the app cancels billing automatically.

lostSales.heading: Sales lost to stock-outs
lostSales.summaryWithRevenue_one: About {{revenue}} ({{units}} units) missed in the last {{days}} days while {{count}} product was out of stock.
lostSales.summaryWithRevenue_other: About {{revenue}} ({{units}} units) missed in the last {{days}} days while {{count}} products were out of stock.
lostSales.summary_one: About {{units}} units missed in the last {{days}} days while {{count}} product was out of stock.
lostSales.summary_other: About {{units}} units missed in the last {{days}} days while {{count}} products were out of stock.
lostSales.how: Estimate: each product's sales rate × its out-of-stock days, at today's selling price.
lostSales.missingPrice_one: {{count}} product has no selling price and is not in the total.
lostSales.missingPrice_other: {{count}} products have no selling price and are not in the total.

purchasePlan.intro: Every order you'll need over the coming weeks if sales keep their current pace, and what it costs, so you can plan cash for stock. Same maths as the reorder suggestions: lead time, safety stock, min/max, minimum order, pack size and each supplier's order cycle. Nothing is saved.
purchasePlan.locked: Plan your orders and stock spending week by week.
purchasePlan.nothing_one: Nothing to order in the next {{count}} week at current sales.
purchasePlan.nothing_other: Nothing to order in the next {{count}} weeks at current sales.
purchasePlan.chartUnits: Units per week (add unit costs to see spend)
purchasePlan.how: Each product sells at its forecast rate; when its stock (with stock on the way) reaches the reorder point, it orders what the forecast suggests, and that order counts as on the way.

discontinued.heading: Discontinued stock
discontinued.summaryWithValue_one: {{count}} discontinued product still holds {{units}} units ({{value}} at cost) to sell through.
discontinued.summaryWithValue_other: {{count}} discontinued products still hold {{units}} units ({{value}} at cost) to sell through.
discontinued.summaryUnits_one: {{count}} discontinued product still holds {{units}} units to sell through.
discontinued.summaryUnits_other: {{count}} discontinued products still hold {{units}} units to sell through.
discontinued.summary: You stopped reordering this product: no order is suggested, and it is left out of alerts and the purchase plan.

accuracy.heading: Forecast accuracy
accuracy.collecting_one: Checking our forecasts takes time: each week we save the forecast and compare it with what really sells over the next {{count}} day. First result on {{date}}.
accuracy.collecting_other: Checking our forecasts takes time: each week we save the forecast and compare it with what really sells over the next {{count}} days. First result on {{date}}.
accuracy.collectingSoon_one: Each week we save the forecast and compare it with what really sells over the next {{count}} day. The first result appears after the first forecast.
accuracy.collectingSoon_other: Each week we save the forecast and compare it with what really sells over the next {{count}} days. The first result appears after the first forecast.
accuracy.noSales: No sales from {{from}} to {{to}} to compare the forecast with.
accuracy.biasHigh: Forecasts were {{percent}} higher than sales overall.
accuracy.biasLow: Forecasts were {{percent}} lower than sales overall.
accuracy.biasNone: No lean toward too high or too low.
accuracy.how_one: Accuracy = 1 − (total forecast miss in units ÷ units sold), counting in-stock days only. Products in stock fewer than {{count}} day, and products whose forecast included bundle sales, are left out.
accuracy.how_other: Accuracy = 1 − (total forecast miss in units ÷ units sold), counting in-stock days only. Products in stock fewer than {{count}} days, and products whose forecast included bundle sales, are left out.
accuracy.bySource_one: Our forecasts: {{computed}}. Your adjusted sales rates ({{count}} product): {{override}}.
accuracy.bySource_other: Our forecasts: {{computed}}. Your adjusted sales rates ({{count}} products): {{override}}.
accuracy.product: Forecast from {{from}} to {{to}}: {{predicted}}/day. Really sold: {{actual}}/day (in-stock days).

events.intro: Tell the forecast about promotions and other known changes in sales (Black Friday, a sale, a holiday closure). Upcoming events raise or lower what to order and when; days of past events count at their normal level, so a sale does not inflate the usual pace.
events.name: Name
events.changeHelp: +100% = double sales, −50% = half. Forecasts are recomputed after saving.
events.emptyBody: Planning a Black Friday or a sale? Add it so orders cover the extra demand in time.
events.confirmDelete: Delete "{{name}}"? Forecasts will be recomputed without it.

orders.markIntroOne: Ordered "{{name}}" outside Shopify (email, phone, a supplier portal)? It will count as on the way, so it is not suggested again.
orders.markIntro_one: {{count}} product ({{units}} units, the suggested quantities) will count as on the way, so they are not suggested again.
orders.markIntro_other: {{count}} products ({{units}} units, the suggested quantities) will count as on the way, so they are not suggested again.
orders.markHelp: Only for orders not entered in Shopify: Shopify purchase orders and transfers already show as on the way.
orders.intro: Orders you placed outside Shopify. While open they count as stock on the way, and for a few days past the expected date in case the delivery is late. Mark them received once the stock is in Shopify.
orders.emptyBody: On the Reorder page, select products and choose "Mark as ordered" after ordering them outside Shopify.
orders.overdueHeading_one: {{count}} order is past its expected date
orders.overdueHeading_other: {{count}} orders are past their expected date
orders.overdueBody: They no longer count as on the way. Mark them received, or cancel them if they will not come.

costs.intro: Stock value, cash tied up, purchase order and plan totals need each product's unit cost. Enter costs here for products without one in Shopify, or to use your real landed cost. They win over Shopify's cost in the app; Shopify itself is not changed.
costs.missingCount_one: {{count}} of {{total}} products has no cost yet.
costs.missingCount_other: {{count}} of {{total}} products have no cost yet.
costs.allSet: Every tracked product has a cost.
costs.importHelp: A CSV with a SKU (or barcode) column and a cost column. A Shopify product export works as is ("Variant SKU", "Cost per item").
costs.importInvalid_one: {{count}} row had a cost we could not read.
costs.importInvalid_other: {{count}} rows had a cost we could not read.
costs.limit: Showing the first {{count}} products (best sellers first). Use search or the file import for the rest.
costs.productFieldHelp: Used for stock value and order totals. Empty = Shopify's cost.
costs.settingsBody: Money figures need a cost per product. Fill in the ones missing in Shopify, one by one or from a file.

budget.intro: Set how much you can spend on stock each month. Everything due now is ranked, most important first, and fills what is left of the budget; the rest waits for next time. Orders you mark as placed this month count as spent.
budget.locked: Set a monthly stock budget and see what to reorder first.
budget.how: Order of priority: out of stock, then products that would run out before a new order arrives, then ABC class A, B, C, then the earliest stock-out. A product that does not fit waits; a cheaper one after it may still fit. Products without a cost are always included.
budget.summaryNoBudget_one: {{count}} product to reorder, {{cost}} in total. Set a budget to see what to order first.
budget.summaryNoBudget_other: {{count}} products to reorder, {{cost}} in total. Set a budget to see what to order first.
